# Project Mirador

> Project Mirador checks a claim, or finds a number, in official U.S. government data and shows the exact source. Free Chrome extension and web page.

Project Mirador is an independent, free fact checker. It is not a government service.

- Web: https://stelthar-api.vercel.app/
- Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/project-mirador/anehbncclhojcaihgeoebennaccpeegn
- About and FAQ: https://stelthar-api.vercel.app/about
- How a claim is judged: https://stelthar-api.vercel.app/methodology
- API for developers: https://stelthar-api.vercel.app/developers
- Privacy: https://stelthar-api.vercel.app/privacy
- Source code: https://github.com/RadoKyselak/Stelthar-API

## How it works

A person highlights a sentence, a paragraph or a whole article in Chrome (right-click, "Check with Project Mirador") or pastes it on the web page. A passage is cut into its claims and each is answered on its own. Project Mirador reads the metric, period and place in the claim, fetches that figure from the agency's own data service, and returns a verdict with the figure and a link to the exact source. It can also look up a number directly and return it with its citation.

## Verdicts

- Supported: the record matches the claim.
- Mostly accurate: the claim is off by a small step in its last digit.
- Misleading: a real figure is used in a way the record does not support.
- Contradicted: the record says otherwise.
- No verdict: no official record covers the claim, and the answer says why.

## Data sources

- Jobs and prices: Bureau of Labor Statistics (unemployment, inflation (CPI), wages, jobs, by state or nationally)
- The economy: Bureau of Economic Analysis (GDP, personal income, trade, government receipts and spending)
- People and places: Census Bureau (population, income, poverty, home values, education, health insurance)
- Federal money: Treasury and USAspending.gov (the national debt, agency budgets and spending by year)
- Laws and votes: Congress.gov and state legislatures (whether a bill passed, the recorded vote, who sponsored it, when it was signed)
- Crime: FBI Crime Data Explorer (violent crime, property crime and murder, by state or nationally)
- Health: CDC and FDA (life expectancy, deaths from COVID-19, overdoses, firearms and other causes, drug approvals, labels and recalls)
- Consumers and housing: FTC and HUD (fraud losses, FTC rules, area median income and income limits)
- Food: USDA FoodData Central (calories and nutrients in a food)
- Other countries: World Bank (population, GDP, unemployment and more for one country)

## Privacy

No accounts, ads, trackers or analytics. Only the text a person chooses to check is sent. The extension cannot read the pages a person visits.
